title: L40S benchmark results + stability notes (Jan 2026)
body:
Doc intent: capture the Jan 2026 L40S benchmark runs and (more importantly) the stability envelope we observed (OOM thresholds, fragmentation behavior, and what concurrency caps feel safe). This is the doc SRE/Infra keep asking for when we say “L40S is fine but you need headroom.”

This is messy / WIP. Numbers are representative, not a marketing artifact.

---

1) Test setup (what we actually ran)

Nodes
- GPU: NVIDIA L40S 48GB (PCIe)
- CPU: 2x sockets (varies by region); we did NOT enforce strict CPU pinning for these runs
- Driver: 550.54.14 (note: one run set was on 545.xx; see anomalies)
- CUDA: 12.4
- Runtime build: runtime main @ ~Jan 20 (pre 1.22 cut); includes early profile pack loader behind flag

Runtime knobs (baseline)
- Scheduler: mixed-workload bucketization OFF for the first week; ON for later runs (see “scheduler=wb1” in table)
- KV cache: default compaction behavior (pre PR-24902); later runs include compaction counters
- Batching: default “aggressive” heuristic initially; we backed off mid-week after seeing p99 issues at higher concurrency (this aligns with the later revert in PR-24988, though that incident was mostly H100)

Models (serving)
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (fp16)
- Llama-3-8B-Instruct (fp16)
- Llama-3-70B-Instruct (4-bit, single GPU is not “prod realistic”, but useful for OOM/fragmentation behavior; results are mostly stability-only)

Workload buckets (bench-lab naming)
- S: prompt 128 / output 128
- M: prompt 512 / output 256
- L: prompt 2k / output 256
- XL: prompt 8k / output 256
- “Mixed”: 40% S, 40% M, 15% L, 5% XL (randomized)

Metrics captured
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (ms)
- scheduler_queue_ms p50/p95 (when available)
- throughput: output tokens/sec (cluster-wide per node)
- GPU util % (avg)
- peak VRAM (GB)
- OOM count (process-level OOM or allocation failure)
- fragmentation estimate (allocator signal; very rough)

---

2) Summary: what we learned (high level)

- L40S is throughput-competitive for smaller models, but it has a tighter stability envelope under bursty/mixed workloads than H100 because VRAM is the binding constraint sooner.
- The “acceptable concurrency” is shaped more by prompt length distribution than raw token rate. Long prefill (L/XL) is the main OOM/fragmentation trigger.
- Fragmentation shows up as: rising allocation retries + compaction time + eventual allocation failure even when “peak VRAM” looks below 48GB. We saw this more when mixing XL requests with small requests at high concurrency.
- Practical safe defaults (for our current allocator + KV cache behavior):
  - For 7B/8B class models: cap concurrency to ~12 for Mixed, ~16 for S/M-only; cap batch tokens (or equivalent) to keep peak VRAM < ~42GB.
  - For any workload with XL present (> ~4k prompt): cap concurrency to ~8 unless you’re comfortable with occasional tail spikes and/or retries.
- We need explicit headroom targets in the profile pack for L40S; “use all memory” is not stable.

---

3) Results table (selected runs)

Conventions
- profile_id: l40s-default-0 (placeholder naming from early profile pack draft)
- scheduler:
  - base = prior scheduler
  - wb1 = workload buckets v1 (post scheduler tuning drop)
- kv:
  - base = old compaction defaults
  - kv1 = compaction thresholds adjusted + counters (post PR-24902-ish; not exactly the final)

Table: 7B/8B perf + stability (all numbers are per node)

Notes on table interpretation
- p99 is end-to-end. When scheduler_queue_ms was enabled (late runs), we saw queueing dominate p99 during the mixed workload at higher conc.
- Peak VRAM > ~45GB correlates strongly with frag + OOM risk for the 8B model when XL exists, even if it doesn’t OOM immediately.

---

4) Stability sweep: OOM thresholds (rough but actionable)

We did a quick sweep increasing concurrency until we hit OOM or allocator failure within ~30 minutes of sustained traffic.

Assumptions
- single node
- no MIG
- typical “Mixed” distribution unless specified

Results (rule-of-thumb)
- Mistral-7B / Llama-3-8B
  - S-only: conc 16 OK (stable), conc 20 = occasional tail blowups but generally no OOM
  - S/M only: conc 16 OK; conc 18 borderline depending on batch heuristic
  - Mixed (incl L + some XL): conc 12 OK; conc 14 borderline; conc 16 not safe (OOM/frag)
  - XL-heavy: conc 6 OK; conc 8 not safe (saw alloc failures + p99 spikes)

- Llama-3-70B (4-bit) “stability-only”
  - Even at conc 1–2, we were near the cliff on some runs. This is not a supported prod target on single L40S; keep it out of default profile docs except as a cautionary note.

What “not safe” means here
- >=1 OOM within 30 minutes OR allocator allocation failure leading to request errors
- We also treated “compaction time exploding + retries” as a warning sign even if it didn’t crash yet.

---

5) Fragmentation behavior (what it looked like)

Observed pattern (most common)
1) Start clean, peak_vram climbs to a steady-state (e.g., 41–44GB) under Mixed.
2) After a few XL requests land, allocator retries increase; compaction time begins to show up (kv1 instrumentation helped).
3) steady-state peak_vram can still look “below 48GB” but allocation failures happen anyway.
4) After failure, restart recovers immediately -> points to fragmentation rather than “true” capacity shortage.

Signals that were predictive (qualitative)
- allocator_fragmentation_estimate trending up for >5 min under mixed
- kv_compaction_ms p95 rising continuously (not spiky)
- sudden increases in scheduler_queue_ms p95 *without* corresponding GPU util increase (system thrashing)

Action item (tracked elsewhere)
- We need to decide what “acceptable frag estimate” is per profile and add an alert in Runtime Profiles dashboard (Allison has a draft spec).

---

6) Recommended L40S defaults (proposed for profile pack v1)

This is what I think should be in the L40S profile as “safe defaults” (not absolute best throughput).

Proposed caps (7B/8B)
- Default concurrency cap (mixed workloads): 12
- If route is explicitly S/M-only (or workload bucket excludes L/XL): allow up to 16
- If XL bucket is present (>= 4k prompts): cap to 8

Memory headroom guidance
- Target peak_vram <= 42GB for “stable, low-incident” operations under mixed.
- Avoid sustained peak_vram > 45GB (becomes “frag roulette”).

Scheduler notes
- Workload buckets v1 (wb1) helped p99 under mixed by reducing queueing spikes.
- However, it can reduce throughput slightly in S-only case (not huge). For L40S, prefer predictable tail.

KV cache / allocator notes
- kv1 seemed to reduce allocator stalls at conc=12 mixed (not definitive).
- We should bias toward earlier compaction / more conservative slab reuse on L40S vs H100.

These align with the intent of PR-24918 (cap default concurrency on L40S) and the follow-up headroom adjustment work (PR-25071).

---

7) Anomalies / reruns needed

- Driver variance: a subset of runs in eu-west were accidentally on driver 545.xx. Those runs had higher kernel fallback and more variance; I excluded most from the “selected runs” table.
- No CPU pinning: we should redo at least one mixed run with recommended CPU/NUMA pinning to understand whether scheduler_queue_ms improves (ENG-4935).
- Noise: tok/s_out fluctuates ~5–10% across time of day. We need more controlled ordering in bench-lab.

---

8) TODO / notes to self

- Add a short “what to tell SRE/oncall” blurb: if you see OOM on L40S pool, first check conc + peak_vram + presence of XL bucket, then consider pinning profile version / reducing concurrency.
- Provide one chart: p99 vs concurrency for Mixed on 8B; right now only table.
- Confirm whether the “safe” conc=12 assumes streaming enabled; if not, call that out.
- Once profile pack naming stabilizes, replace l40s-default-0 with real profile_id/profile_version.
